**Target:** Background, Decisions [CORRECTION], R4, T-2, Clarifications, Acceptance Criteria
**Issue:** The current registry contains 68 leaves: 67 shared leaves (including 36 run leaves) plus query. The spec also states 66 shared, run 35, and 65 canonical paths.
**Required change:** Align every fixed count to 67 shared, 1 query, 68 total, and 36 run leaves, removing the contradictory 66/35/65 references.
**Why blocking:** The implementation and completeness matrix cannot determine whether all current leaves, including recover-spec-gate-repair, are in scope; tests could pass while omitting a real command.

finding.body:
**Target:** R1-R3; src/flow/registry.js; src/lib/command-registry.js; src/help.js
**Issue:** FLOW_COMMANDS currently stores option names in flags/options arrays, while placeholders, aliases, and descriptions are embedded in free-form help strings. Existing flowOptions() reverse-parses only Options sections and misses entries whose option text is inline. The spec forbids reverse-parsing help prose but does not provide structured metadata for all leaf options or define how localized/prose text is retained.
**Required change:** Require each shared leaf to declare complete structured option metadata—canonical name, aliases, kind, placeholder, description, and localization policy—in the designated registry/model, with command prose kept separately.
**Why blocking:** Without an explicit source, implementation must either reverse-parse forbidden prose or invent/drop option metadata, making parser/help identity and preservation tests impossible to implement deterministically.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec requires structured option metadata and separately retained prose in R1-R3, matching the supplied source review; these requirements are actionable corrections rather than resolved or invalid findings.

finding.body:
**Target:** R4-R6 P/Z definitions and boundary matrix; src/flow/lib/get-runtime-log.js; src/flow/lib/get-issue.js; src/flow/lib/set-issue.js; src/flow/lib/set-init.js
**Issue:** The spec requires P/Z to be safe integers and requires unsafe or zero values to be rejected. Existing owners do not share that contract: runtime-log converts arbitrary positive digit strings to Number without a safe-integer check, get-issue accepts zero and unbounded digits, set-issue uses parseInt without a safe bound, and set-init checks Number.isInteger rather than Number.isSafeInteger.
**Required change:** Replace the blanket P/Z contract with the verified per-owner contracts, or explicitly authorize and target validator changes for every affected command.
**Why blocking:** The required rejection matrix conflicts with current accepted input and the stated compatibility/no-new-admission constraints, so implementation and tests cannot simultaneously preserve behavior and satisfy R4-R6.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec applies one universal P/Z safe-integer matrix while its cited command owners have distinct contracts; R4-R6 therefore need owner-backed corrections before implementation.

finding.body:
**Target:** R4/R5 set issue-log inventory; R6 D; src/flow/lib/set-issue-log.js
**Issue:** The spec classifies --repair-ref-commit as D, defined as a lowercase 64-hex digest. The existing owner accepts a commit hash matching /^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$/i, including uppercase and lengths that D rejects.
**Required change:** Classify --repair-ref-commit using the existing commit-hash contract and reserve D for actual 64-hex digests, or explicitly scope a compatible owner change.
**Why blocking:** The generated contract would reject existing valid commit references and accept values the owner rejects, changing a preserved CLI input path and invalidating the required matrix.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec classifies set issue-log --repair-ref-commit as a lowercase 64-hex digest, while the supplied owner evidence identifies a different existing commit-hash contract; the R4-R6 contract must be corrected.

finding.body:
**Target:** R4 inventory vs R5 leaf contract for set issue-log --guardrail-candidate
**Issue:** R4 declares --guardrail-candidate as ID, while R5 declares it as T. The existing owner treats it as free-form text and applies an owner-specific minimum length, not identifier validation.
**Required change:** Use one owner-backed class consistently, namely T plus the existing owner-specific length rule, throughout the inventory and validation sections.
**Why blocking:** The parser/model and tests have contradictory acceptance expectations for the same option, and applying ID validation would reject the existing free-text contract.
finding.evidence: The immutable Spec contains the stated R4/R5 type conflict for set issue-log --guardrail-candidate, so the owner-backed T contract needs a coordinated correction.
